items.title: Victoria's health debate shouldn't stop at the hospital door
items.summary: Five days before Victorians vote, an argument that both parties' ED pledges treat the hospital as the whole health system.

_homepage.note: Labor is promising $1.5 billion and a 25% expansion of a dozen emergency departments; the Coalition is promising transit lounges. Croakey's point is that neither addresses what puts people in the department in the first place, which is the part that actually changes ED load. This is the system he works inside being argued over in the week it gets decided — the election is 28 November.

items.title: Once Human's Dissonant Resonance season releases
items.summary: Season five landed a day early and builds its combat around rhythm, including a four-player fight against a pipe-organ colossus.

_homepage.note: The feed carried the PlayStation Blog's co-op boss showcase ahead of this; here is what actually shipped on the Visional Wheel servers. Rewards include a deviation pet granting cycling buffs and gear with new damage-boosting suffixes, which is the detail that decides whether a season is worth re-rolling for. Worth a look while Dragonwilds sits quiet until December's Luminance update.

items.title: SGEM#526: Stayin' Alive with Bicarb for IHCA?
items.summary: A placebo-controlled trial finally tests the bicarb ampoule that gets pushed in arrests on reflex, and it does not hold up.

_homepage.note: Sustained ROSC came out at 39% versus 37% against placebo — a difference that disappears into the noise, which makes this a drug to stop reaching for rather than one to time better. Guest skeptic Gillian Schmitz works it through the SGEM's structured appraisal, so you get the trial's weaknesses rather than just its headline. In-hospital arrest is the one resus setting where the drug trolley is always within reach, which is exactly why the reflex needs the evidence checked.

items.title: First GTA 6 PS5 Patch Live Now, Get All the Details Here
items.summary: Four days after launch, the first actual patch notes — crashes, autosave, stuck weather, and the Wanted Level bug.

_homepage.note: A 603.8MB download rolling out in stages, so it may not have reached his console yet. The fixes are the unglamorous launch-week kind: autosave failures, phone calls not triggering, weather locking for hours, and a bug that stopped players losing their Wanted Level. The feed already has the launch and the PS5 Pro performance breakdown, so this is the next real data point on how the PS5 version is actually holding up.

items.title: Freestyle Records Covers Lost UK Street Soul, Brit Funk and Boogie
items.summary: The British end of the reissue-label world he already buys from, and a map of where to start.

_homepage.note: Freestyle has been digging up UK funk, soul and dancefloor jazz since 2003 — the same job Colemine, Big Crown and Athens of the North do for the American side, all of which the collection and this feed already lean on. Brit funk and street soul are the gap on that shelf: adjacent to the Sharon Jones and Menahan Street Band records, but with a different rhythm section lineage. A label guide is the efficient way in when you do not know a single catalogue number yet.

items.title: Franklin & Poe and 3sixteen Mark 10 Years in 17oz Neppy Selvedge
items.summary: A heavyweight anniversary make-up where the neppy yarn is the whole point, not a finish applied afterwards.

_homepage.note: Neps are slubs of unevenly spun cotton left in the yarn deliberately, so the texture is woven in and shows up as the indigo wears rather than being sanded on at the factory. At 17oz this is the weight class above the Wonder Looper and Fullcount pieces the feed has already carried, and the retailer-plus-maker anniversary format usually means a one-run fabric. $310 at Franklin & Poe.

items.title: Celebrating 20 Years of Strut, Whose Compilations Span the Globe
items.summary: The compilation label that connects the funk shelf to the world-music shelf, profiled at its twentieth year.

_homepage.note: Strut's range runs from disco, soul and funk to African music and post-punk, which is unusually close to how the collection is actually split across genres — the Buena Vista Social Club and Gipsy Kings end sitting beside James Brown and Parliament. Compilations are how you buy into a scene you have no reference points for, and Strut's are the well-curated kind rather than the licensing-grab kind. Note the date: this is a twentieth-anniversary piece, so treat the catalogue as having grown since.

items.title: Does Panscanning Stable Trauma Patients Improve Outcomes?
items.summary: The haemodynamically stable trauma patient is the one where the pan-scan decision is actually yours, and this is the evidence for making it.

_homepage.note: Published today, and it targets the gap between what trauma guidelines imply and what the outcome data supports for patients who are not crashing. The selective-imaging argument matters at registrar level because you are the one justifying the scan to radiology at 3am. Pairs directly with the blunt cerebrovascular injury and penetrating rectal injury pieces already in the feed — same question of how much imaging a stable trauma patient earns.

items.title: Wishbone: Chris Lucas's New Hong Kong Diner
items.summary: Opens tomorrow — three levels of 1960s Hong Kong diner off Bourke Street, with a karaoke room on top.

_homepage.note: Dan Chan, born in Hong Kong, is running the kitchen, and the detail worth going for is prawn toast built on yau char gwai rather than sliced bread. Yum cha starts on weekends next year, so the dim sum service is the reason to go now rather than wait. Entry is via the McKillop Street laneway at 435 Bourke Street — a city trip rather than a northside walk, but the Lucas group's openings book out fast.

items.title: NoKings — My 2026 photo of the year
items.summary: Art Meripol picks a protest frame as his year's best, which makes this the one photo-of-the-year entry about photographing an event rather than a mood.

_homepage.note: The 35mmc photo-of-the-year run has mostly produced quiet, personal frames — the winter gardens and still lifes already in the feed. This one is documentary work made in a crowd, where you get one exposure and no second attempt, and the write-up is about that constraint rather than the camera. Useful counterweight if the series has started to feel like the same photograph twelve times.
